citation: Clarke, B., Baker, S., Smolkowski, K., Doabler, C., Strand Cary, M., & Fien, H. (2015). Investigating the efficacy of a core kindergarten mathematics curriculum to improve student mathematics learning outcomes. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 8(3), 303-324. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2014.980021
report_number: DOI 10.1080/19345747.2014.980021; J. Res. Educ. Eff. 8(3):303-324; ERIC EJ1068562; IES Award R305A080699 (Early Learning in Mathematics)
design: Cluster-randomized controlled trial; assignment level = Teacher/Class (129 kindergarten classrooms randomly assigned WITHIN schools to ELM treatment [68 classrooms] vs business-as-usual standard district math instruction [61 classrooms], blocking on school and full/half-day schedule). 46 schools across two states/cohorts (Oregon 2008-09, Texas 2009-10); 2,598 students (1,401 ELM, 1,197 control). Intervention = Early Learning in Mathematics (ELM), a 120-lesson Tier-1 core whole-class kindergarten math curriculum (number/operations, geometry, measurement, vocabulary); ELM teachers received teacher professional development (initial 2-4h logistics meeting plus three 4-hour ELM curriculum trainings across fall/winter/spring covering lesson content and explicit-instruction teacher behaviors). Subject = mathematics; grade = kindergarten (registry band K-2). Outcomes: TEMA-3 and EN-CBM (fall pretest, spring K posttest) and SAT-10 Problem Solving + Procedures (winter grade 1 follow-up). Analyzed with SAS PROC MIXED multilevel models (students nested in classrooms), all tests on 126 df.
problems: Verified title/authors/year directly from the on-disk PDF (see notes). The paper reports Hedges' g directly in Table 4 for each full-sample condition effect, so g values are taken verbatim from the paper. The study found NO statistically significant overall condition effect on any outcome (TEMA Time x Condition p=.0517, EN-CBM p=.1463, SAT-10 PS p=.8911, SAT-10 Procedures p=.7853); the only significant finding was a moderation of the TEMA effect by initial achievement (Table 5, TEMA x Time x Condition p=.0039), favoring students below the 25th percentile -- that is a subgroup/interaction result, not a full-sample mean contrast. The abstract's p=.0039 and SAT p=.9737/.6336 refer to those Table-5 moderation terms, NOT the full-sample condition contrasts. g_se/g_var below are computed from the spec's large-sample approximation using analyzed n_t/n_c; the multilevel model's SE for each impact estimate is recorded in impact_se but is in the raw test metric (not the g metric). ICCs (design-effect, from Table 4) are recorded per outcome; the reported g and SE come from the multilevel impact model so cluster_adjusted=true. n_t/n_c are the analyzed sample sizes at the relevant timepoint (Table 3): T2 (K spring posttest) = 1134 ELM / 982 control for TEMA and EN-CBM; T3 (grade-1 winter follow-up) = 893 ELM / 788 control for SAT-10.

effect_sizes.arm_label: ELM curriculum + teacher PD vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.test_name: Test of Early Mathematics Ability, Third Edition (TEMA-3), raw score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring of kindergarten, T2; immediate post-intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g taken directly from Table 4 (paper computed g = 0.108 for the Time x Condition gain-difference fixed effect, the change from fall pretest to spring posttest). g_var/g_se from spec large-sample approximation Var(d)=(nt+nc)/(nt*nc)+g^2/(2*(nt+nc)), Var(g)=J^2*Var(d), J=1-3/(4*126-1)=0.99404, using T2 analyzed n. Raw-metric impact estimate 1.08 (SE 0.55) standardized by paper to g.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.315 Table 4 (g and p in 'Time x Condition' row); means/SDs p.314 Table 3
effect_sizes.notes: Primary conceptual-understanding outcome. Full-sample condition effect; not statistically significant (p=.0517). The TEMA effect was significantly moderated by initial achievement (Table 5) favoring low-pretest students, but that is a subgroup/interaction result, not extracted here as a full-sample contrast. Time coded 0=T1,1=T2; Condition 0=control,1=ELM.
